## The part tutorials skip {.smaller}

::: {.kicker}
Beyond fork · clone · branch · commit · push
:::

Most people learn how to make commits. Almost no one learns how to keep
a repository and its history clean.

Three small habits do most of the work:

. . .

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
### gitignore
**Prevent** the mess.
Stop junk from ever entering the repo.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
### git stash
**Avoid** the mess.
Set work aside without a junk commit.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
### git rebase
**Fix** the mess.
Rewrite messy commits into clean ones.
:::
:::

. . .

> Prevent it, avoid it, or fix it, and your history stays readable.

---

## 1 · `.gitignore` {.smaller}

::: {.kicker}
Prevent the mess
:::

A plain text file that tells Git which files to **never track**.
You commit *code*, not the things around it:

. . .

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Data** — `*.csv`, `*.parquet`, raw datasets
- **Secrets** — `.env` files, API keys
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Build output** — `_site/`, `__pycache__/`
- **Artifacts** — trained models, large binaries
:::
:::

. . .

```bash
# .gitignore  →  lives at the root of your repo
*.csv                 # data stays out of version control
.env                  # never commit credentials
__pycache__/          # Python noise
/_site/  /.quarto/    # Quarto build output
```

. . .

> A leaked key or a 2 GB file buried in history is *painful* to undo.
> Prevention always beats cleanup.

---

## 2 · `git stash` {.smaller}

::: {.kicker}
Avoid the mess
:::

You're mid-edit when something urgent pulls you to another branch.
Your changes aren't ready to commit. What now?

. . .

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### ✗ The messy way
```bash
git commit -m "WIP dont look"
```
A throwaway commit that clutters
history forever.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### ✓ The clean way
```bash
git stash      # set aside
git checkout main
git stash pop  # bring back
```
Your work is parked safely, then
restored untouched.
:::
:::

. . .

```{=html}
<div class="terminal">
  <div class="term-bar">
    <span class="dot red"></span>
    <span class="dot yellow"></span>
    <span class="dot green"></span>

<div><span class="prompt">~/portfolio (feature) $</span> <span class="cmd">git stash pop</span>      <span class="comment"># bring it right back</span></div>

  </div>
</div>
```

## 3 · `git rebase -i` {.smaller}

::: {.kicker}
Fix the mess
:::

Real working history is honest, and honestly *ugly*:

```bash
* a1b2c3d  fix typo again
* d4e5f6g  oops forgot import
* h7i8j9k  WIP
* p3q4r5s  add customer dedup logic
```

. . .

No reviewer wants to read *"oops"* and *"WIP"*. Interactive rebase lets
you rewrite these before anyone sees them:

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~4     # edit the last 4 commits
```

. . .

In the editor, change `pick` to `squash` to fold commits together:

```bash
pick   p3q4r5s  add customer dedup logic
squash h7i8j9k  WIP
squash d4e5f6g  oops forgot import
squash a1b2c3d  fix typo again
```

---

## The payoff {.smaller}

::: {.kicker}
Fix the mess
:::

Four noisy commits become **one** you'd be proud to ship:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Before
```bash
* fix typo again
* oops forgot import
* WIP
* add dedup logic
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
### After
```bash
* Add customer dedup
  logic with null
  handling + tests
```
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-warning}
Golden rule: rebase only commits you **haven't shared** yet.
Rewrite local history freely, but never rewrite `main`.
:::

. . .

> A clean history is a gift to your reviewer, and to *future you*.

### Thank you
